To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
IT investment decision makers in Egypt are not fully aware of the importance of Technology Acceptance as a behavioral dimension in IT investment evaluation.
IT decision makers in Egypt do not consider technology acceptance in their IT investment decisions.
IT BSC is a suitable framework to evaluate IT investments and that Technology Acceptance is a key factor in such decisions.
In summary, our research is concerned with

two main issues: (1) the extent that IT investment decisions are affected by Technology Acceptance and (2) the extent that users in general and in Egypt in particular are willing to use IT based systems.

the development of a theoretical framework for IT investment evaluation, which is based on the Balanced Scorecard (BSC) concept and incorporates the behavioral dimension represented by the Unified Theory of Acceptence and Use of Technology.
the development of a theoretical framework that can be used to evaluate IT investments in Egypt based on IT BSC.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
decision makers in IT investments decisions are aware that IT investments are not always successful, but they are not aware of what are the reasons behind such failure.
decision makers do not account for Technology Acceptances in IT investment decisions, and this is a major gap in the literature.

IT BSC is not used in Egypt in its original form, rather, IT BSC is extended by decision makers in Egypt with additional dimensions and variables to suit the local context, which is not a bad thing in itself, however, the extent that these dimensions are used is not clear and needs further investigation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have extended IT BSC to include Behavioral Dimension represented by UTAUT and updated UTAUT to account for relevant variables and beliefs.
the proposed framework is not only theoretically and practically sound but also it is practically applicable.

this paper proposes a framework that extends the IT BCS to account for behavioral dimension represented by UTAUT, which is not considered in IT BSC, and it also extends the UTAUT by taking into consideration other variables and beliefs that were not considered by the original UTAUT model.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, the decision makers in Egypt do not take technology acceptance into consideration in their IT investment decisions, and they do not account for behavioral dimension in their IT BSC.
IT BSC is not a complete tool to evaluate IT Investments.
, the proposed framework is a good starting point for future research and practical applications.
